newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Most LatAm stocks seen continuing upwards in week.
newsitem.headline: Most LatAm stocks seen continuing upwards in week.

text.p: Most Latin American stock markets are seen continuing their upward trend this week with Chile being the exception because of drought that threatens to dry up profits in the electricity sector, dealers said.
Brazilian dealers said shares there were likely to be led by benchmark Telebras, as investors return to the market after last week's U.S. Thanksgiving holiday.

Brazilian telecoms stocks were seen rising on expectations a telecomunications bill would go to Congress. Hopes the government would make progress on a new round of tariff adjustments was also positive, they said.
"There's a rumor that there will be a single tariff hike, rather than several small ones," said Marco Sa of Banco Geral do Comercio brokerage.

Optimism also was seen up this week on brighter prospects for President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's bid to stand for re-election in 1998. The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index rose 0.3 percent last week to end at 66,661 points. Mexico's IPC index, after gaining 0.10 percent last week, will likely test the 3,300-point barrier this week in a year-end rally on an expected domestic rate cut and probable bargain-hunting by foreign investors, traders said.

Nevertheless, dealers said they expected a decline in the U.S. Dow Jones Industrial Average from its recent high levels, which could prompt the Mexican index to retreat towards a consolidation band of 3,200 to 3,250 points.
Argentine stocks were seen heading cautiously up, after the Merval index rose 8.17 percent in November.

"The market is going to start a new week on an upward path, but with a certain amount of caution today considering the advance on Friday and above all because the market is very close to its highs of the year," said Gustavo Galffione, a trader at Velox investments.
The Merval rose 2.22 percent Friday to 617.03 points, very close to this year's high of 619.37 points set on May 21.
Banco Credito Argentino analysts said the next resistance level for the Merval is 620 index points, while its support is at 600.
Dealers are upbeat in the face of economic recovery signs.
"The recovery of Argentina's economy is generating great expectations," said Norman Trabucco, of brokers Zaracan.
Venezuelan share prices were seen broadly stable, with a slight upward tendency, in moderate trade as the market begins to wind down for the holiday period.

In Venezuela, the Caracas Stock Exchange received a boost from the announcement of a one-for-six share dividend in Electricidad de Caracas. The market's 19-share index slipped 0.4 percent to 6,189.12 last week.
Electricidad, long the benchmark stock on the exchange, could gradually see its position as market leader usurped by national telephone company CANTV, whose shares began trading in earnest last week.
In Chile, after a string of losses last week, stocks are expected to continue retreating this week on slides in the heavyweight electricity sector, traders said.
"We still see some weakness in the market...the mood is unsettled," said Lance Eckel, of the Sud Americano brokerage.

Electricity stocks, which have a 40 percent weighting in the selective IPSA index, have tumbled in recent weeks over fears that a serious drought this year in central Chile will hurt company fourth-quarter earnings, dealers said.
"Investors are depressed over the energy sector and how the drought issue is affecting Endesa," Eckel said.

Hydro-electric generators like power giant Endesa are having to buy in expensive electricity from outside producers as water levels in their own dams are too low to generate enough power to meet their commitments.
Heavy losses in the power sector dragged down the market last week, with the IPSA index losing 3.33 percent to close at 92.64 points.
- Buenos Aires Newsroom, 541 318-0650
